units.zh: 徐延旭，字曉山，山東臨清人。
units.en: Xu Yanxu, whose courtesy name was Xiaoshan, came from Linqing in Shandong.
units.literal: Xu Yanxu, style name Xiaoshan, was a man of Linqing in Shandong.

units.zh: 咸豐十年進士，出知廣西容縣。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of the Xianfeng reign and was appointed magistrate of Rong County in Guangxi.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he became a jinshi and was sent out as magistrate of Rong County in Guangxi.

units.zh: 師克潯州，與有功，累晉知府。
units.en: When government forces took Xunzhou, he distinguished himself in the campaign and rose step by step to the rank of prefect.
units.literal: When the army captured Xunzhou he had a share in the merit and was repeatedly promoted to prefect.

units.zh: 同治九年，除知梧州。
units.en: In the ninth year of Tongzhi he was made prefect of Wuzhou.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Tongzhi he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou.

units.zh: 光緒三年，遷安襄荊鄖道。
units.en: In the third year of Guangxu he was transferred to the An-Xiang-Jing-Yun circuit.
units.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was transferred to the An-Xiang-Jing-Yun circuit intendancy.

units.zh: 八年，晉廣西布政使，命督辦海防，得專奏事。
units.en: In the eighth year he was promoted to treasurer of Guangxi, put in charge of coastal defense, and allowed to memorialize the throne directly.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Guangxi provincial treasurer, ordered to supervise coastal defense, and granted the right to submit memorials on his own authority.

units.zh: 時法人謀佔全越，巡撫張之洞、侍讀張佩綸先後疏薦堪軍事。
units.en: The French were then seeking to occupy all of Vietnam, and Governor Zhang Zhidong and Hanlin reader Zhang Peilun both memorialized the court in turn, commending him as capable in military matters.
units.literal: At the time the French were plotting to seize all of Vietnam; Governor Zhang Zhidong and Hanlin reader Zhang Peilun successively memorialized recommending him as fit for military affairs.

units.zh: 會南定陷，朝命出鎮南關，與提督黃桂蘭、道員趙沃籌防，未行，越官劉永福戰勝懷德府紙橋，狀其績以上。
units.en: When Nam Dinh fell, the court ordered him to take command at Zhennan Pass and work out defenses with Brigadier Huang Guilan and Circuit Intendant Zhao Wo. Before he marched, the Vietnamese commander Liu Yongfu defeated the enemy at Paper Bridge in Hoa Duc prefecture and sent up a report of his victory.
units.literal: When Nam Dinh fell, the court ordered him out to guard Zhennan Pass and plan defense with Brigadier Huang Guilan and circuit intendant Zhao Wo; before he set out, the Vietnamese official Liu Yongfu won a battle at Paper Bridge in Hoa Duc prefecture and reported his achievements upward.

units.zh: 九年，出關，至北寧而還，頓龍州，被命為巡撫，敕趣永福規河內。
units.en: In the ninth year he crossed the border, advanced as far as Bac Ninh, then withdrew and encamped at Longzhou. He was appointed governor and instructed to press Liu Yongfu to move against Hanoi.
units.literal: In the ninth year he went through the pass, went as far as Bac Ninh and returned, and halted at Longzhou; he was appointed governor and ordered to urge Yongfu to march on Hanoi.

units.zh: 延旭上部署防守狀，略云：「固廣西邊疆，必守北寧；
units.en: Yanxu memorialized the court with a plan for the defense, stating in brief: 'To hold the Guangxi border secure, Bac Ninh must be defended;
units.literal: Yanxu submitted a memorial on the deployment of defense, saying in summary: 'To secure the Guangxi frontier, Bac Ninh must be held;

units.zh: 固雲南邊疆，必守山西。
units.en: to hold the Yunnan border secure, Son Tay must be defended.
units.literal: to secure the Yunnan frontier, Son Tay must be held.

units.zh: 左軍前鋒分駐北寧、湧球，去城止十二里。
units.en: The left army's advance units were encamped at Bac Ninh and Yongqiu, a mere twelve li from the city.
units.literal: The vanguard of the left army was posted separately at Bac Ninh and Yongqiu, only twelve li from the city.

units.zh: 一旦有事，援之則無辭於法，聽之則有慚於越。
units.en: If fighting broke out, sending aid would give France grounds for complaint, yet standing by would shame us before Vietnam.
units.literal: If trouble arose, to reinforce them would give the French a pretext, while to leave them alone would bring shame before Vietnam.

units.zh: 不如徙軍入城，城固我儲糧屯戍所也。
units.en: Better to pull the troops into the city, which was in any case our storehouse and garrison base.
units.literal: It would be better to move the troops into the city, for the city was after all our depot for grain storage and garrison.

units.zh: 並簡銳扼浪泊湖北岸，為山西聲援；
units.en: At the same time he proposed posting picked troops on the north bank of Lang Bo Lake to support Son Tay;
units.literal: At the same time select crack troops to hold the north bank of Lang Bo Lake as a supporting force for Son Tay;

units.zh: 別募勇百人扼月德江，與陸軍相表裡。」
units.en: and raising a separate company of a hundred braves to hold the Nguyet Duc River, working in concert with the main army.'
units.literal: and separately raise a hundred braves to hold the Nguyet Duc River, coordinating with the land forces inside and out.'

units.zh: 附請吏部主事唐景崧留軍。
units.en: He also asked that Tang Jingsong of the Ministry of Personnel be retained with the forces.
units.literal: He also asked that Tang Jingsong, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, be kept with the army.

units.zh: 初，法人犯順安，越未敗，遽乞和。
units.en: Earlier, when the French attacked Thuan An, Vietnam had not yet been beaten but still rushed to sue for peace.
units.literal: Earlier, when the French attacked Thuan An, Vietnam had not yet been defeated but hastily sued for peace.

units.zh: 延旭奏言：「越人倉卒議和，或謂因故君未葬，冀緩須臾；
units.en: Yanxu reported: 'The Vietnamese rushed into peace talks. Some said they hoped only to buy time because the late king had not yet been buried;
units.literal: Yanxu memorialized: 'The Vietnamese hastily negotiated peace; some said it was because the late ruler had not yet been buried and they hoped to gain a brief respite;

units.zh: 或謂因廢立嫌疑，朋興黨禍。
units.en: others said factions were exploiting doubts over the succession and whipping up partisan strife.
units.literal: others said it was because of suspicion over deposition and succession, with factions stirring up partisan strife.

units.zh: 越臣黃佐炎等錄寄和約，越誠無以保社稷，中國又何以固籓籬？
units.en: Minister Huang Zuoyan and others forwarded a copy of the treaty. If Vietnam could not truly preserve its throne, how was China to hold its frontier barrier firm?
units.literal: The Vietnamese minister Huang Zuoyan and others sent a transcript of the peace treaty; if Vietnam truly could not preserve its altars of state, how could China secure its frontier barrier?

units.zh: 劉永福現駐山西，法人擬益師往攻，請毋撤兵，用警戎備。」
units.en: Liu Yongfu was then at Son Tay, and the French were preparing reinforcements for an attack. He asked that our troops not be withdrawn, so that defenses might stay on alert.'
units.literal: Liu Yongfu was then stationed at Son Tay; the French planned to send more troops to attack, and he asked that troops not be withdrawn so as to keep military readiness on alert.'

units.zh: 越王阮福升嗣位，遣使告哀，並懇允其詣闕乞封；
units.en: The new king Nguyen Phuc Thang sent envoys to announce his accession and begged leave for a mission to the imperial court to seek investiture;
units.literal: King Nguyen Phuc Thang of Vietnam succeeded to the throne, sent envoys to announce mourning, and also begged permission for him to come to court to request investiture;

units.zh: 复具和約二十七條及黃佐炎禀，上之樞府。
units.en: he also forwarded the twenty-seven articles of the peace treaty together with Huang Zuoyan's report to the Grand Council.
units.literal: he also submitted the twenty-seven articles of the peace treaty together with Huang Zuoyan's report, forwarding them to the Grand Council.

units.zh: 左宗棠檄前布政使王德榜募勇扼桂邊，朝命受延旭節度。
units.en: Zuo Zongtang ordered former Provincial Treasurer Wang Debang to raise troops and hold the Guangxi frontier, and the court placed him under Yanxu's command.
units.literal: Zuo Zongtang ordered the former provincial treasurer Wang Debang to raise braves and hold the Guangxi border; the court commanded that he accept Yanxu's command.

units.zh: 其冬，力疾再出關，駐諒山，趣軍進取，分襲海陽、嘉林綴敵勢；
units.en: That winter, ill as he was, he crossed the border again and took post at Lang Son. He pressed the army to advance and sent columns to strike Hai Duong and Gia Lam and tie down the enemy.
units.literal: That winter, forcing himself despite illness, he again went through the pass, stationed himself at Lang Son, urged the army forward, and sent detachments to raid Hai Duong and Gia Lam to pin down the enemy;

units.zh: 並請撥船嚴扼海口，斷其出入：諭仍力守北寧。
units.en: He also asked for vessels to block the river mouth and cut the enemy's lines of supply. The court told him nonetheless to hold Bac Ninh at all costs.
units.literal: he also asked that ships be assigned to block the estuary strictly and cut off enemy movement in and out: the court instructed him still to hold Bac Ninh firmly.

units.zh: 於是令左軍黃桂蘭、右軍趙沃協防其地。
units.en: He then ordered Huang Guilan's left wing and Zhao Wo's right wing to defend the place together.
units.literal: Thereupon he ordered Huang Guilan of the left army and Zhao Wo of the right army to defend the place jointly.

units.zh: 適山西陷，延旭猶慮兵力薄，復遣使入關募勇，通舊五十餘營，厚集於此。
units.en: Son Tay had just fallen, and Yanxu still feared his forces were too few. He sent men back through the pass to raise troops and gathered more than fifty former battalions in strength there.
units.literal: Just then Son Tay fell; Yanxu still feared his forces were thin, and again sent envoys back through the pass to raise braves, mustering more than fifty old battalions in strength at this point.

units.zh: 隨令廣間諜，安地營，禁擾民，嚴冒餉；
units.en: He spread spies widely, ordered camps properly sited, forbade harassment of civilians, and cracked down hard on padded payrolls.
units.literal: He then ordered extensive use of spies, proper siting of camps, prohibition of harassment of the people, and strict punishment of false muster rolls;

units.zh: 然沃等皆寡識，桂蘭尤侈汰，與越官張登壇日事宴樂。
units.en: Yet Zhao Wo and his fellows were shallow men, and Huang Guilan was especially extravagant. He and the Vietnamese official Zhang Dengtan spent their days in feasting and pleasure.
units.literal: Yet Zhao Wo and the others were all men of little judgment; Huang Guilan was especially extravagant and wasteful, and with the Vietnamese official Zhang Dengtan feasted and made merry every day.

units.zh: 登壇故通法，嗣以有郤洩其事。
units.en: Dengtan had long been in touch with the French; later, after a falling-out, he betrayed the fact.
units.literal: Dengtan had formerly been in contact with the French; later, because of a rift, he leaked the matter.

units.zh: 上命延旭罷登壇，或囚而殺之，延旭以力不能制而止。
units.en: The throne ordered Yanxu to remove Dengtan, or to imprison and execute him, but Yanxu desisted because he lacked the power to enforce it.
units.literal: The emperor ordered Yanxu to dismiss Dengtan, or imprison and execute him; Yanxu stopped because he had not the power to control him.

units.zh: 日唯籌軍火濟師，以為兵力厚，可恃以無恐。
units.en: He spent his days only arranging arms and supplies for the troops, convinced that with so large a force he had nothing to fear.
units.literal: Day after day he only planned arms and supplies to support the army, thinking that with thick forces he could rely on them without fear.

units.zh: 桂蘭復希風指，侈談部下能戰，延旭益信之，遂六上書請戰。
units.en: Huang Guilan again tried to read his commander's mind and boasted of his men's fighting power. Yanxu believed him all the more and six times memorialized asking permission to give battle.
units.literal: Huang Guilan again sought to read his superior's wishes and boasted that his subordinates could fight; Yanxu believed him all the more and six times submitted memorials requesting battle.

units.zh: 上不許，敕保守未失陷地，毋貪功。
units.en: The emperor refused and ordered him to hold whatever ground had not yet been lost and not court glory recklessly.
units.literal: The emperor did not permit it and ordered him to hold what had not yet fallen and not seek merit greedily.

units.zh: 十年，法軍陷扶良，三路攻北寧，桂蘭潰奔太原。
units.en: In the tenth year the French took Phu Luong and attacked Bac Ninh on three fronts. Huang Guilan's force collapsed and fled toward Thai Nguyen.
units.literal: In the tenth year the French army took Phu Luong, attacked Bac Ninh on three routes, and Huang Guilan broke and fled to Thai Nguyen.

units.zh: 李鴻章電奏失守，延旭猶上言：「西聯滇軍，東防江口，北寧斷無他虞。」
units.en: Li Hongzhang telegraphed that the position had been lost, yet Yanxu still reported: 'With the Yunnan army on our west and the river mouth guarded on the east, Bac Ninh is surely in no danger.'
units.literal: Li Hongzhang telegraphed reporting the loss of the position; Yanxu still memorialized: 'In the west we are linked with the Yunnan army, in the east we guard the river mouth; Bac Ninh certainly has no other worry.'

units.zh: 上責其飾詞。
units.en: The emperor rebuked him for dressing up the truth.
units.literal: The emperor rebuked him for glossing over the facts.

units.zh: 會岑毓英抵保勝，部署邊外各軍，遂命延旭軍屬之。
units.en: When Cen Yuying reached Baosheng and took charge of the frontier armies, Yanxu's forces were placed under his command.
units.literal: When Cen Yuying reached Baosheng and deployed the various armies beyond the border, the court then placed Yanxu's army under his command.

units.zh: 初，延旭之任西撫也，未及兩月，亦知桂蘭等未可恃。
units.en: When Yanxu first took up the governorship of the western provinces, he had known within two months that Huang Guilan and his like were not to be trusted.
units.literal: At first, when Yanxu took office as governor of the western provinces, before two months had passed he too knew that Huang Guilan and the others could not be relied on.

units.zh: 嗣以臨敵易將，操之急，易生變，以故誥誡備至；
units.en: Later, knowing that replacing commanders on the eve of battle or driving them too hard could easily spark mutiny, he issued repeated stern admonitions.
units.literal: Later, because replacing generals on the eve of battle and pressing them too hard easily produced mutiny, for that reason he admonished them at length in edicts;

units.zh: 而桂蘭等且縱兵剽奪，越民不堪命，忿滋甚。
units.en: Yet Huang Guilan and his men still let their troops loot and pillage until the Vietnamese could bear no more and their anger grew fierce.
units.literal: yet Huang Guilan and the others also let their troops plunder and seize; the Vietnamese people could not bear it and their resentment grew ever worse.

units.zh: 是役也，群反噬，城乃陷。
units.en: In that battle the populace turned on them, and the city fell.
units.literal: In this campaign the masses turned on them in retaliation, and the city then fell.

units.zh: 延旭上其欺飾狀，並自糾請治罪。
units.en: Yanxu reported their deceit and filed a confession of his own, asking to be punished.
units.literal: Yanxu reported their deception and concealment and also impeached himself, requesting punishment.

units.zh: 上怒，詔革職留任。
units.en: The emperor was furious and stripped him of rank while leaving him in his post.
units.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered him dismissed from office but retained in his post.

units.zh: 法軍乘勝入芹驛關，復命力扞之，毋再失。
units.en: The French pressed their victory into Qinyi Pass, and he was again ordered to hold the line and lose no more ground.
units.literal: The French army pressed its victory into Qinyi Pass, and he was again ordered to defend it firmly and lose no more ground.

units.zh: 延旭以景崧護軍收殘兵，更約束，令駐屯梅。
units.en: Yanxu put Jingsong in charge of gathering the shattered troops, restoring discipline, and posting them at Tunmei.
units.literal: Yanxu had Jingsong protect the army, gather the broken remnants, impose discipline anew, and order them stationed at Tunmei.

units.zh: 時諒江、朗山、狼甲相繼屠潰，諒山教民且蠢焉思動。
units.en: Lang Giang, Lang Son, and Lang Giap had been overrun in turn, and the Christian converts in Lang Son were already stirring.
units.literal: At the time Lang Giang, Lang Son, and Lang Giap were slaughtered and routed in succession, and the Christian converts of Lang Son were also stirring restlessly.

units.zh: 延旭鑑覆轍，嚴禁防軍向越官索夫米，有伐一草一木者斬，越民仍不知感。
units.en: Learning from past disasters, Yanxu strictly forbade frontier troops to demand porters and grain from Vietnamese officials and ordered death for anyone who so much as cut grass or wood, yet the Vietnamese still showed no gratitude.
units.literal: Yanxu, taking warning from the repeated disaster, strictly forbade the frontier troops to demand laborers and grain from Vietnamese officials; anyone who cut a single blade of grass or tree was beheaded, yet the Vietnamese still did not feel gratitude.

units.zh: 適德榜至，勸延旭勉自支振，圖再舉。
units.en: Wang Debang then arrived and urged Yanxu to rally himself and plan a fresh campaign.
units.literal: Just then Wang Debang arrived and urged Yanxu to brace himself and plan another effort.

units.zh: 於是更嚴勒粵軍，仿楚勇制，力求後效。
units.en: He tightened discipline on the Guangdong troops further still, modeled them on the Hunan braves, and strove for better results.
units.literal: Thereupon he tightened discipline on the Guangdong army still further, modeled it on the Hunan braves system, and strove for results later.

units.zh: 而逮問之命下，吏議斬監候，改戍新疆。
units.en: Then came the order for his arrest and trial. The officials first recommended execution after imprisonment, then commuted the sentence to exile in Xinjiang.
units.literal: But the order for arrest and trial came down; the officials recommended decapitation after imprisonment, changed to banishment to Xinjiang.

units.zh: 追論舉主，之洞、佩綸，均被訶責。
units.en: Those who had recommended him, Zhidong and Peilun, were both sharply rebuked in turn.
units.literal: Tracing responsibility to those who had recommended him, Zhidong and Peilun were both severely reprimanded.

units.zh: 延旭未出都，病卒。
units.en: Yanxu died of illness before he could leave the capital.
units.literal: Yanxu had not yet left the capital when he died of illness.

units.zh: 子坊，自有傳。
units.en: His son Fang is treated in a separate biography.
units.literal: His son Fang has a separate biography.

units.zh: 唐炯，字鄂生，貴州遵義人。
units.en: Tang Jiong, whose courtesy name was Esheng, came from Zunyi in Guizhou.
units.literal: Tang Jiong, style name Esheng, was a man of Zunyi in Guizhou.

units.zh: 道光二十九年舉人，訓方子。
units.en: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang and was the son of Tang Xunfang.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he became a provincial graduate; he was the son of Tang Xunfang.

units.zh: 訓方督師金口，炯馳數千里省視。
units.en: When his father commanded the army at Jinkou, Jiong rode thousands of li to see him.
units.literal: Instructor Tang commanded the army at Jinkou; Jiong raced several thousand li to visit him.

units.zh: 越夕難作，倉皇奉遺疏謁曾國籓，得代奏。
units.en: Disaster struck the very next night. He hurried off with his father's final memorial to Zeng Guofan, who had it presented to the throne in his stead.
units.literal: The next night disaster struck; in haste he carried the final memorial and called on Zeng Guofan, who submitted it on his behalf.

units.zh: 武昌复，求遺骸歸葬。
units.en: When Wuchang was recovered, he recovered his father's remains for burial at home.
units.literal: When Wuchang was recovered, he sought his father's remains for burial at home.

units.zh: 桐梓亂民起，治鄉團御之。
units.en: When rebels rose in Tongzi, he organized local militia to hold them off.
units.literal: When rebellious commoners rose in Tongzi, he organized local militia to resist them.

units.zh: 服闋，入貲為知縣，銓四川。
units.en: After his mourning period he purchased appointment as magistrate and was assigned to Sichuan.
units.literal: When mourning was ended, he purchased office as magistrate and was assigned by selection to Sichuan.

units.zh: 咸豐六年，署南溪。
units.en: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Nanxi.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Nanxi.

units.zh: 值滇寇李永和蠢動，藍朝柱應之，陷敘州，吏士皆恐。
units.en: The Yunnan rebel Li Yonghe was on the move, and Lan Chaozhu joined him. They took Xuzhou, and officials and gentry alike were terrified.
units.literal: It happened that the Yunnan bandit Li Yonghe stirred up trouble and Lan Chaozhu answered him; they took Xuzhou, and officials and gentry were all afraid.

units.zh: 炯乃訓練兵壯，晨夜徼循，人心稍靖。
units.en: Jiong drilled the militia, patrolled day and night, and gradually restored calm among the people.
units.literal: Jiong then trained militia, patrolled morning and night, and popular sentiment gradually calmed.

units.zh: 有為寇所獲者，縱之還，曰：「為我語唐青天，決不犯南溪一草一木！」
units.en: A man captured by the bandits was sent back with the message: 'Tell Blue-Sky Tang for us—we will not touch so much as a blade of grass in Nanxi!'
units.literal: Someone captured by the bandits was released and sent back with the message: 'Tell Blue-Sky Tang for us: we will certainly not violate a single blade of grass or tree in Nanxi!'

units.zh: 炯領兵偪吊黃樓，單騎入營，諭以利害，朝柱款附。
units.en: Jiong led his troops against Diaohuang Tower, rode alone into the rebel camp, explained the stakes, and Chaozhu surrendered.
units.literal: Jiong led troops to press Diaohuang Tower, entered the camp alone on horseback, explained advantage and harm, and Chaozhu submitted in good faith.

units.zh: 永和改犯犍為，炯馳救，壁不動，俟其懈乘之，寇狂奔，自相轔藉。
units.en: Yonghe turned to attack Qianwei. Jiong rushed to the rescue, held his walls fast, and when the enemy slackened struck at once. The rebels broke and fled, trampling one another in their panic.
units.literal: Yonghe then shifted to attack Qianwei; Jiong raced to the rescue, held his walls without moving, waited until they slackened and struck, and the bandits fled in wild confusion, trampling one another.

units.zh: 旋與楚軍解成都圍。
units.en: Soon afterward he joined the Hunan army in lifting the siege of Chengdu.
units.literal: Shortly afterward, together with the Hunan army, he lifted the siege of Chengdu.

units.zh: 八年，檄署綿州事。
units.en: In the eighth year he was ordered to serve as acting prefect of Mianzhou.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered by dispatch to act as prefect of Mianzhou.

units.zh: 時郫、彭軍事棘，調還省防守。
units.en: Fighting at Pi and Peng had grown desperate, and he was recalled to defend the provincial capital.
units.literal: At the time military affairs in Pi and Peng were critical, and he was transferred back to the provincial capital for defense.

units.zh: 炯诇得黑窩盜虛實，請限八日畢乃事，果如所言。
units.en: Jiong scouted the Heiwowo bandits and learned their true strength. He asked for eight days to finish the job, and finished exactly when he said he would.
units.literal: Jiong reconnoitered and learned the true state of the Heiwowo bandits, asked for a limit of eight days to finish the affair, and it turned out exactly as he said.

units.zh: 除知夔州，未上，踰月，永和圍綿城，炯掘壕登陴，民助貲糧。
units.en: He was appointed prefect of Kuizhou but had not yet taken up the post when, a month later, Yonghe besieged Mian City. Jiong dug trenches and manned the walls, and the people supplied money and grain.
units.literal: He was appointed prefect of Kuizhou but had not yet taken up the post when, after a month, Yonghe besieged Mian City; Jiong dug trenches and mounted the battlements, and the people helped with funds and grain.

units.zh: 炯居城三月，不下，誓死守；
units.en: Jiong held the city for three months without yielding and swore to die before surrendering.
units.literal: Jiong held the city for three months without yielding and swore to defend it to the death;

units.zh: 援至，圍始解。
units.en: Relief arrived at last and the siege was broken.
units.literal: when relief arrived, the siege was finally lifted.

units.zh: 已而湘、黔軍閧州署，駱秉章劾罷之。
units.en: Soon afterward Hunan and Guizhou troops rioted at the prefectural yamen, and Luo Bingzhang impeached him and had him removed.
units.literal: Before long the Hunan and Guizhou armies rioted at the prefectural yamen; Luo Bingzhang impeached and dismissed him.

units.zh: 事白，仍治軍。
units.en: When the matter was cleared, he returned to military command.
units.literal: When the matter was cleared, he was again put in charge of troops.

units.zh: 同治改元，統安定營。
units.en: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign he took command of the Anding battalion.
units.literal: When the Tongzhi reign began, he commanded the Anding battalion.

units.zh: 會石達開圍涪州，與劉岳昭期會師，擊走之。
units.en: When Shi Dakai besieged Fuzhou, he joined Liu Yuezhao in a coordinated attack and drove him off.
units.literal: When Shi Dakai besieged Fuzhou, he arranged a joint campaign with Liu Yuezhao and drove him off.

units.zh: 其夏，石黨窺綦江。
units.en: That summer Shi's followers probed Qijiang for weakness.
units.literal: That summer, Shi's followers watched for an opening at Qijiang.

units.zh: 炯聞警馳援，燔其壁，寇潰，大破之長寧。
units.en: Hearing the alarm, Jiong rushed to reinforce, burned their stockade, routed them, and won a great victory at Changning.
units.literal: Jiong heard the alarm and raced to reinforce, burned their stockade, the bandits broke, and he inflicted a great defeat on them at Changning.

units.zh: 以疾還成都。
units.en: Illness forced him back to Chengdu.
units.literal: Because of illness he returned to Chengdu.

units.zh: 秉章詢寇勢，時寇退滇邊，聲入黔，炯曰：「此誘我軍東下耳。
units.en: Bingzhang asked about the rebels. They had withdrawn toward the Yunnan border while spreading word into Guizhou. Jiong said: 'This is a feint to draw our army east.
units.literal: Bingzhang asked about the bandit situation; the bandits had then retreated to the Yunnan border and their fame entered Guizhou; Jiong said: 'This is to lure our army eastward.

units.zh: 彼必走夷地，乘虛入川，寧越宜警備。」
units.en: They will surely slip through the Yi lands and strike into Sichuan when we are exposed. Ningyuan and Yuexi should be on guard.'
units.literal: They are sure to go by the Yi country routes and enter Sichuan by seizing an opening; Ningyuan and Yuexi should be put on alert.'

units.zh: 俄而寇入紫地，复請遣唐友耕軍大渡河扼之。
units.en: Soon the rebels entered Zidi, and he again asked that Tang Yougeng's army be sent to block them at the Dadu River.
units.literal: Before long the bandits entered Zidi, and he again asked that Tang Yougeng's army be sent to hold them at the Dadu River.

units.zh: 達開返西岸，退為倮夷所窘，食盡乞降，梟誅之。
units.en: Dakai recrossed to the west bank, was harried by the Lolo tribes as he retreated, ran out of food, and begged to surrender. He was beheaded and his head displayed.
units.literal: Dakai returned to the west bank, retreated and was pressed by the Lolo tribes, his food ran out and he begged to surrender, and he was executed by decapitation and display.

units.zh: 明年，權綏定府，區邑為八路，路若干場，場若干寨，置寨總，行記善惡法，月朔上其簿親判之；
units.en: The next year he served as acting prefect of Suiding. He divided the prefecture into eight routes, each route into districts and each district into stockades, appointed stockade chiefs, and instituted a register of good and bad conduct, personally reviewing the monthly ledgers on the first of each month.
units.literal: The next year he acted as prefect of Suiding, divided the districts into eight routes, each route into several chang, each chang into several stockades, appointed stockade chiefs, and carried out a register of good and evil conduct, personally judging the ledgers submitted on the first of each month;

units.zh: 又立書院二、社學八十餘：境內稱治，下其法他縣。
units.en: He also founded two academies and more than eighty village schools. The region was said to be well governed, and his methods were adopted in other counties.
units.literal: he also established two academies and more than eighty village schools: within the jurisdiction order was praised, and his methods were extended to other counties.

units.zh: 越二年，赴陝佐治營田。
units.en: Two years later he went to Shaanxi to help administer military colonies.
units.literal: After two years he went to Shaanxi to assist in managing military colonies.

units.zh: 捻首張總愚犯新豐，大敗之。
units.en: When the Nian leader Zhang Zongyu attacked Xinfeng, Jiong inflicted a crushing defeat on him.
units.literal: The Nian leader Zhang Zongyu attacked Xinfeng and was heavily defeated.

units.zh: 六年，四川總督崇實命率師入黔。
units.en: In the sixth year Sichuan Governor Chongshi ordered him to lead troops into Guizhou.
units.literal: In the sixth year Sichuan Governor Chongshi ordered him to lead an army into Guizhou.

units.zh: 黔患貧瘠，崇實先問以理財策，炯曰：「理財莫若節用，節用莫若裁勇，裁勇莫若援黔。」
units.en: Guizhou was poor and exhausted. Chongshi first asked his advice on finances. Jiong said: 'The best way to manage finances is to cut spending; the best way to cut spending is to trim the braves; and the best way to trim the braves is to pacify Guizhou.'
units.literal: Guizhou suffered from poverty and barrenness; Chongshi first asked him for a policy on managing finances, and Jiong said: 'To manage finances nothing is better than economizing; to economize nothing is better than cutting braves; to cut braves nothing is better than aiding Guizhou.'

units.zh: 崇實然其言，遂以軍事屬之。
units.en: Chongshi approved and placed the military campaign in his hands.
units.literal: Chongshi approved his words and thereupon entrusted military affairs to him.

units.zh: 連破偏刀、水上、大平、黃飄、白堡，擒斬王超凡、劉儀順，降潘人傑、唐天佑，皆積寇也；
units.en: He took Piandao, Shuishang, Daping, Huangpiao, and Baibao in succession, captured and executed the veteran rebels Wang Chaofan and Liu Yishun, and accepted the surrender of Pan Renjie and Tang Tianyou.
units.literal: He successively broke Piandao, Shuishang, Daping, Huangpiao, and Baibao, captured and executed Wang Chaofan and Liu Yishun, and received the surrender of Pan Renjie and Tang Tianyou, all long-standing bandits;

units.zh: 又克平越、甕安、黃平、清平、麻哈：遷道員，賜號法克精阿巴圖魯。
units.en: He also captured Pingyue, Weng'an, Huangping, Qingping, and Mahai. He was promoted to circuit intendant and granted the title Fakejing A Batulu.
units.literal: he also took Pingyue, Weng'an, Huangping, Qingping, and Mahai: he was promoted to circuit intendant and granted the title Fakejing A Batulu.

units.zh: 嗣為吳棠所劾，還蜀。
units.en: Later Wu Tang impeached him, and he returned to Sichuan.
units.literal: Later he was impeached by Wu Tang and returned to Sichuan.

units.zh: 光緒四年，丁寶楨督四川，令佐治鹽筴，旋補建昌道。
units.en: In the fourth year of Guangxu, when Ding Baozhen became governor of Sichuan, he put Jiong in charge of the salt administration and soon afterward appointed him to the Jianchang circuit.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu Ding Baozhen governed Sichuan, ordered him to assist in managing the salt monopoly, and shortly afterward he was appointed to the Jianchang circuit.

units.zh: 六年，署鹽茶道，條上善後六事，謂：「發引必先新後舊；
units.en: In the sixth year he served as acting salt and tea intendant and submitted six measures for reform, stating: 'Transport permits must be issued for new salt before old;
units.literal: In the sixth year he acted as salt and tea circuit intendant and submitted in detail six measures for rehabilitation, saying: 'In issuing transport permits, the new must come before the old;

units.zh: 徵稅必先課後引；
units.en: taxes must be assessed before permits are issued;
units.literal: in collecting taxes the assessment must come before the permit;

units.zh: 收發鹽引，責成鹽道；
units.en: issuing and receiving transport permits should be the salt intendant's responsibility;
units.literal: in issuing and receiving salt transport permits, responsibility should rest with the salt circuit;

units.zh: 改代引張，責成州縣；
units.en: replacing substitute permit agents should be the responsibility of prefectures and counties;
units.literal: in changing substitute permit agents, responsibility should rest with prefectures and counties;

units.zh: 繳殘則嚴定限期；
units.en: surrender of unused permits should be subject to strict deadlines;
units.literal: in surrendering unused permits, strict deadlines should be fixed;

units.zh: 辦公則優給公費。」
units.en: and officials should receive generous public funds for their work.'
units.literal: in conducting official business, generous public funds should be provided.'

units.zh: 議行，凡百餘年引目渾殽、款項轇轕諸弊，至是盡革，語具鹽法志。
units.en: The measures were adopted. Abuses of more than a century—confused permit records, tangled accounts, and the like—were swept away at last, as recorded in the monograph on salt administration.
units.literal: The measures were adopted and put into practice; abuses of more than a hundred years, such as confused permit records and tangled accounts, were at this point entirely reformed, as set forth in detail in the monograph on the salt laws.

units.zh: 八年，張之洞、張佩綸先後奏薦堪軍事，於是擢雲南布政使。
units.en: In the eighth year Zhang Zhidong and Zhang Peilun both recommended him for military command, and he was promoted to treasurer of Yunnan.
units.literal: In the eighth year Zhang Zhidong and Zhang Peilun successively memorialized recommending him as fit for military affairs, and he was thereupon promoted to Yunnan provincial treasurer.

units.zh: 炯率川軍千人駐關外，滇軍悉歸節度。
units.en: Jiong led a thousand Sichuan troops beyond the border pass, and all Yunnan forces were placed under his command.
units.literal: Jiong led a thousand Sichuan troops stationed beyond the pass, and all Yunnan forces were placed under his command.

units.zh: 既蒞事，裁夫馬，治廠務，並釐卡，清田糧，民困少蘇。
units.en: Once in office he cut porter and transport levies, reorganized the mining administration, consolidated transit stations, and cleared land-tax accounts, so that the people's burdens eased somewhat.
units.literal: Once he took up affairs, he cut porters and horses, managed the mining works, consolidated transit stations, cleared land-tax accounts, and popular hardship was somewhat relieved.

units.zh: 法人奪我越南，被命赴開化防守，即於軍前除巡撫。
units.en: When the French seized Vietnam from China, he was ordered to Kaihua on defense duty and was appointed governor on the spot before the army.
units.literal: The French seized our Vietnam; he was ordered to go to Kaihua to defend, and was at once appointed governor before the army.

units.zh: 誤聞將議和，亟還省履任。
units.en: Mistakenly hearing that peace talks were imminent, he hurried back to the provincial capital to take up his duties.
units.literal: Mistakenly hearing that peace was about to be negotiated, he hurried back to the province to take up his post.

units.zh: 上大怒，褫職逮問，刑部定讞斬監候。
units.en: The emperor was furious, stripped him of rank, and ordered his arrest. The Ministry of Justice sentenced him to decapitation after imprisonment.
units.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, stripped him of office and ordered arrest and trial; the Ministry of Justice fixed the sentence as decapitation after imprisonment.

units.zh: 久之，上意解，三歷秋審，赦歸。
units.en: In time the emperor relented. After three autumn sentence reviews he was pardoned and sent home.
units.literal: After a long time the emperor's anger eased; through three autumn reviews he was pardoned and returned home.

units.zh: 左宗棠臚其治行上於朝，命戍雲南，交岑毓英差序。
units.en: Zuo Zongtang memorialized the court on his administrative record. He was ordered to serve in Yunnan and placed at Cen Yuying's disposal.
units.literal: Zuo Zongtang set forth his record of administration and submitted it to the court; he was ordered to serve exile in Yunnan and placed under Cen Yuying's assignment.

units.zh: 十三年，賞巡撫銜，督辦雲南礦務，偕日本礦師躬履昭通、東川、威寧銅鉛各廠，疏陳變通章程，又歷請減免貴州鉛課，豁免雲南礦廠官欠民欠，並報可。
units.en: In the thirteenth year he was given governor's rank and put in charge of Yunnan mining. With Japanese mining engineers he personally inspected the copper and lead works at Zhaotong, Dongchuan, and Weining, submitted revised regulations, and repeatedly asked for cuts in Guizhou lead taxes and cancellation of official and private debts at Yunnan mines—all approved.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he was granted the rank of governor, supervised Yunnan mining affairs, and together with Japanese mining engineers personally inspected the copper and lead works at Zhaotong, Dongchuan, and Weining; he memorialized in detail revised regulations, and also repeatedly requested reduction of Guizhou lead levies and exemption of official and private debts owed by Yunnan mines, all of which were approved.

units.zh: 惟經營十五年，僅歲解京銅百萬斤，為時論所譏。
units.en: Yet after fifteen years of management he forwarded only a million jin of copper a year to the capital, and contemporary opinion mocked the result.
units.literal: Yet in fifteen years of management he forwarded only a million jin of copper annually to the capital, and was ridiculed in contemporary opinion.

units.zh: 三十一年，謝病歸。
units.en: In the thirty-first year he retired on grounds of illness.
units.literal: In the thirty-first year he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

units.zh: 三十四年，以鄉舉重逢，晉太子少保。
units.en: In the thirty-fourth year, on the fiftieth anniversary of his provincial examination, he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, because he had passed the provincial examination fifty years earlier, he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 逾歲卒，年八十，卹如製。
units.en: He died the following year at eighty, and state mourning was granted according to regulation.
units.literal: The following year he died at the age of eighty; mourning rites were granted according to regulation.

units.zh: 何璟，字小宋，廣東香山人。
units.en: He Jing, whose courtesy name was Xiaosong, came from Xiangshan in Guangdong.
units.literal: He Jing, style name Xiaosong, was a man of Xiangshan in Guangdong.

units.zh: 父曰愈，見循吏傳。
units.en: His father Yu is treated in the biographies of model officials.
units.literal: His father was named Yu and appears in the biographies of model officials.

units.zh: 璟，道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，轉御史。
units.en: Jing passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and later became a censor.
units.literal: Jing, a jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and transferred to censor.

units.zh: 咸豐七年，英人陷廣州，總督葉名琛獲譴罷，而巡撫柏貴等罪相埒，譴弗及，時論譁然，璟乃分別上其謬誤狀。
units.en: In the seventh year of Xianfeng the British took Guangzhou. Governor Ye Mingchen was punished and dismissed, yet Governor Bai Gui and others were equally guilty yet went unpunished, and public opinion was outraged. Jing memorialized separately on each man's errors.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng the English took Guangzhou; Governor Ye Mingchen was punished and dismissed, yet Governor Bai Gui and others were guilty to the same degree but were not punished, and public opinion was in an uproar; Jing thereupon submitted separate memorials on their errors.

units.zh: 明年，英艦入津沽，疏陳戰守要略，先後抗論外務，疏凡八上。
units.en: The next year, when British ships entered Tientsin, he memorialized on the essentials of war and defense and argued repeatedly against foreign-policy concessions, submitting eight memorials in all.
units.literal: The next year, when British ships entered Tientsin, he memorialized on essentials of war and defense, and successively argued against foreign affairs policy, submitting eight memorials in all.

units.zh: 遷給事中。
units.en: He was promoted to supervising secretary.
units.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary.

units.zh: 十年，出為安徽廬鳳道。
units.en: In the tenth year he was appointed Lu-Feng circuit intendant in Anhui.
units.literal: In the tenth year he went out as Lu-Feng circuit intendant of Anhui.

units.zh: 同治二年，遷按察使。
units.en: In the second year of Tongzhi he was made provincial judge.
units.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he was transferred to provincial judge.

units.zh: 捻至，與總兵喻吉三隨方應禦，寇不得逞。
units.en: When the Nian rebels appeared, he and Brigadier Yu Jisan met them wherever they struck, and the rebels could not break through.
units.literal: When the Nian arrived, together with Brigadier Yu Jisan he responded wherever needed and the bandits could not prevail.

units.zh: 四年，晉湖北布政使。
units.en: In the fourth year he was promoted to treasurer of Hubei.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Hubei provincial treasurer.

units.zh: 逾歲，到官，值黃陂飢嗛，民就食江、漢，便宜發帑金濟之。
units.en: A year later he took up his post. Huangpi was in famine, and people were fleeing to the Yangzi and Han for food. He promptly disbursed treasury funds for relief.
units.literal: After a year he reached his post; it happened that Huangpi suffered famine, and the people sought food along the Yangzi and Han rivers; he promptly disbursed treasury funds to relieve them.

units.zh: 九年，擢福建巡撫，歷山西、江蘇。
units.en: In the ninth year he was made governor of Fujian and later served in Shanxi and Jiangsu.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to governor of Fujian, and served successively in Shanxi and Jiangsu.

units.zh: 遭父憂，服闋，起閩浙總督。
units.en: After his father's death and the mourning period, he was recalled as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
units.literal: He suffered his father's death; when mourning ended he was recalled as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

units.zh: 光緒三年，備日本議起，治海防，飭戎政。
units.en: In the third year of Guangxu, with negotiations with Japan impending, he strengthened coastal defense and tightened military administration.
units.literal: In the third year of Guangxu, as negotiations with Japan were impending, he managed coastal defense and tightened military administration.

units.zh: 其夏患水祲，日坐城上督拯難民，凡閱七晝夜，醵金卹之。
units.en: That summer floods struck. For seven days and nights he sat on the city wall directing relief for refugees and raised funds for their care.
units.literal: That summer there was flood disaster; day after day he sat on the city wall supervising relief for refugees, for seven days and nights in all, and raised funds to comfort them.

units.zh: 水退，濬洪塘江，導支流入海，後患稍殺。
units.en: When the waters receded he dredged the Hongtang River and channeled branch streams to the sea, easing future flood risk.
units.literal: When the water receded, he dredged the Hongtang River and channeled branch streams to the sea, and later troubles were somewhat reduced.

units.zh: 五年，兼署巡撫。
units.en: In the fifth year he also served as acting governor.
units.literal: In the fifth year he also acted as governor.

units.zh: 時日本議廢琉球，數以兵艦浮閩、滬。
units.en: Japan was then pressing to abolish the Ryukyu kingdom, and repeatedly sent warships to cruise off Fujian and Shanghai.
units.literal: At the time Japan was negotiating abolition of the Ryukyu kingdom, and repeatedly sent warships to cruise off Fujian and Shanghai.

units.zh: 璟以台灣地當要衝，基隆尤扼全台形勝，乃調集輪舶，增募兵勇，建築砲台，備不虞。
units.en: Jing held that Taiwan was strategically vital and that Keelung commanded the island's key terrain. He assembled steam vessels, raised more troops, built batteries, and prepared against surprise attack.
units.literal: Jing held that Taiwan occupied a critical position and Keelung especially commanded the strategic advantage of the whole island; he thereupon assembled steam vessels, increased recruitment of troops, built batteries, and prepared against the unexpected.

units.zh: 九年，法越事起，海防戒嚴。
units.en: In the ninth year the Franco-Vietnamese conflict broke out and coastal defenses were placed on alert.
units.literal: In the ninth year the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose and coastal defense was placed on alert.

units.zh: 璟令總兵張得勝等分扼諸郡，提督孫開華等分扼台、澎，並檄楊在元署台灣鎮，助防守。
units.en: Jing ordered Brigadier Zhang Desheng and others to hold the prefectures and Brigadier Sun Kaihua and others to hold Taiwan and Penghu. He also put Yang Zaiyuan in acting command of the Taiwan garrison to assist in the defense.
units.literal: Jing ordered Brigadier Zhang Desheng and others to hold the various prefectures in separate detachments, and Brigadier Sun Kaihua and others to hold Taiwan and Penghu; he also dispatched Yang Zaiyuan to act as Taiwan commander to assist in defense.

units.zh: 明年，又上福、廈、台益船募卒狀，上皆勗勵之。
units.en: The next year he memorialized again on adding ships and recruiting troops for Fujian, Xiamen, and Taiwan, and the emperor commended him warmly.
units.literal: The next year he again submitted a memorial on increasing ships and recruiting soldiers for Fujian, Xiamen, and Taiwan; the emperor encouraged him in all respects.

units.zh: 已而會辦軍務，張佩綸至，事皆專決，視璟等若屬吏；
units.en: Soon he was assigned to joint management of military affairs. Zhang Peilun arrived, decided everything himself, and treated Jing and the others as mere subordinates.
units.literal: Before long he was assigned to joint management of military affairs; Zhang Peilun arrived, decided everything on his own authority, and treated Jing and the others as subordinate officials;

units.zh: 又嚴劾在元貪謬，璟坐疏忽，幹吏議。
units.en: He also impeached Zaiyuan for corruption and incompetence. Jing was held negligent and referred to the personnel office for deliberation.
units.literal: he also sternly impeached Zaiyuan for corruption and folly; Jing was implicated for negligence and referred to the personnel office for deliberation.

units.zh: 以是益畏事之，不敢為異同。
units.en: Jing feared him all the more and dared not disagree.
units.literal: For this reason Jing feared him all the more in affairs and did not dare to differ.

units.zh: 佩綸調舟師砲船局，璟亦以砲布衙署自衛。
units.en: Peilun transferred the fleet to the gunboat bureau. Jing also posted cannon around his yamen for self-defense.
units.literal: Peilun transferred the naval force to the gunboat bureau; Jing also placed cannon around his yamen for self-defense.

units.zh: 廷旨以閩事亟，諄諄諭固守。
units.en: Because Fujian affairs were urgent, the court repeatedly ordered him to hold firm.
units.literal: Court edicts, because Fujian affairs were urgent, repeatedly instructed him to hold firm.

units.zh: 逮戰書至，璟告佩綸曰：「明日法人將乘潮攻馬尾矣！」
units.en: When war was declared, Jing told Peilun: 'Tomorrow the French will attack Mawei on the tide!'
units.literal: When the declaration of war arrived, Jing told Peilun: 'Tomorrow the French will attack Mawei on the tide!'

units.zh: 佩綸弗聽。
units.en: Peilun would not listen.
units.literal: Peilun would not listen.

units.zh: 舟師大挫，璟欲馳援，而臨浦無舟可濟，株守省城，卒致閩事日壞；
units.en: The fleet was crushed. Jing wanted to rush to reinforce them, but there were no boats at Linpu to cross the river. He stayed fixed in the provincial capital, and Fujian affairs grew worse by the day.
units.literal: The fleet suffered a great defeat; Jing wished to rush to reinforce but at Linpu there were no boats to cross, and he remained fixed at the provincial capital, until Fujian affairs grew worse day by day;

units.zh: 然猶左袒廣勇，雖逃不問，頗為時訾議。
units.en: He still favored the Guangdong braves and did not punish deserters, which drew considerable public censure.
units.literal: yet he still favored the Guangdong braves and did not inquire into deserters, which drew considerable censure in contemporary opinion.

units.zh: 乃飛章自劾，而廷旨已先召還京。
units.en: He sent an urgent memorial impeaching himself, but the court had already ordered him back to the capital.
units.literal: He then sent an urgent memorial impeaching himself, but a court edict had already recalled him to the capital.

units.zh: 尋御史亦劾其闒冗，部議褫職。
units.en: Soon a censor impeached him for slackness and incompetence, and the ministry recommended stripping him of office.
units.literal: Shortly afterward a censor also impeached him for slackness and incompetence, and the ministry recommended stripping him of office.

units.zh: 十四年，卒。
units.en: He died in the fourteenth year.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.

units.zh: 張兆棟，字友山，山東濰縣人。
units.en: Zhang Zhaodong, whose courtesy name was Youshan, came from Weixian in Shandong.
units.literal: Zhang Zhaodong, style name Youshan, was a man of Weixian in Shandong.

units.zh: 道光二十五年進士，銓刑部主事，累遷郎中。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, entered the Ministry of Punishments as a principal clerk, and rose to director.
units.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, he was selected as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and was repeatedly promoted to director.

units.zh: 出知陝西鳳翔府，蒞事三月，而回寇竊發，乃募鄉兵捍之。
units.en: He was appointed prefect of Fengxiang in Shaanxi. Three months after taking office Hui rebels rose, and he raised local militia to resist them.
units.literal: He went out as prefect of Fengxiang in Shaanxi; three months after taking office the Hui rebels broke out in secret, and he raised local militia to resist them.

units.zh: 無何，城被圍，寇且掘長壕圖久困，兆棟晨夕登陴慰勞守者。
units.en: Before long the city was besieged. The rebels dug a long trench to starve it out. Zhaodong mounted the walls morning and evening to encourage the defenders.
units.literal: Before long the city was besieged; the rebels were also digging a long trench intending prolonged encirclement; Zhaodong morning and evening mounted the battlements to comfort and encourage the defenders.

units.zh: 寇轟潰西南城，蟻附上，兆棟躬冒矢石，戰甚力，寇不得逞。
units.en: The rebels breached the southwest wall and swarmed up like ants. Zhaodong fought in the thick of the arrows and stones, and the rebels could not break through.
units.literal: The rebels battered and breached the southwest wall; they swarmed up like ants; Zhaodong personally braved arrows and stones and fought fiercely, and the rebels could not prevail.

units.zh: 益固結紳民，誓堅守，閱十有六月，援師至，圍始解。
units.en: He rallied the gentry and people, swore to hold out, and after sixteen months relief arrived and the siege was broken.
units.literal: He further strengthened ties with gentry and people, swore to hold firm, and after sixteen months relief troops arrived and the siege was finally lifted.

units.zh: 超授四川按察使。
units.en: He was exceptionally promoted to provincial judge of Sichuan.
units.literal: He was exceptionally promoted to Sichuan provincial judge.

units.zh: 咸豐四年，調廣東，遷布政使。
units.en: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Guangdong and made provincial treasurer.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Guangdong and promoted to provincial treasurer.

units.zh: 左宗棠治軍嘉應​​，餽運阻絕，兆棟殫心籌畫，給食不乏。
units.en: When Zuo Zongtang commanded the army at Jiaying, supply lines were cut. Zhaodong threw himself into planning, and the troops never went hungry.
units.literal: When Zuo Zongtang commanded the army at Jiaying, supply transport was cut off; Zhaodong exhausted himself in planning and provisions did not run short.

units.zh: 歷安徽、江蘇，皆稱職。
units.en: He served in Anhui and Jiangsu and was praised in both posts.
units.literal: He served in Anhui and Jiangsu, and in both was said to perform his duties well.

units.zh: 九年，擢漕運總督。
units.en: In the ninth year he was promoted to director-general of grain transport.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to director-general of grain transport.

units.zh: 時運河久廢不緝，兆棟慮海警阻漕，為上治河濟運狀，稱旨。
units.en: The Grand Canal had long gone without dredging. Fearing that naval threats would block grain transport, Zhaodong submitted a memorial on river management to keep supplies moving, and the emperor approved it.
units.literal: At the time the Grand Canal had long gone without dredging; Zhaodong feared that naval alarms would block grain transport and submitted to the emperor a memorial on managing the river to aid transport, which met with approval.

units.zh: 十一年，再調廣東。
units.en: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Guangdong again.
units.literal: In the eleventh year he was again transferred to Guangdong.

units.zh: 粵俗嗜博，闈姓害尤烈，疏請禁止，報可，而總督英翰曲徇商人請，弛其禁，兆棟劾之，落職，遂兼攝總督事，禁益嚴，終其任，粵吏無敢言闈姓者。
units.en: Guangdong was addicted to gambling, and the examination-surname lottery was especially ruinous. He memorialized for a ban and won approval, but Governor Yinghan bent to the merchants and relaxed it. Zhaodong impeached him, Yinghan was dismissed, and Zhaodong took over as acting governor. The ban was enforced more strictly than ever, and for the rest of his term no Guangdong official dared mention the lottery again.
units.literal: Guangdong custom was addicted to gambling; the harm of the examination-surname lottery was especially severe; he memorialized requesting prohibition and received approval, but Governor Yinghan bent to merchants' requests and relaxed the ban; Zhaodong impeached him, Yinghan was dismissed from office, and Zhaodong then concurrently acted as governor; the prohibition grew stricter, and to the end of his term no Guangdong official dared speak of the examination-surname lottery.

units.zh: 光緒四年，母憂歸。
units.en: In the fourth year of Guangxu he returned home to mourn his mother.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he returned home on his mother's death.

units.zh: 服闋，起福建巡撫。
units.en: After mourning he was recalled as governor of Fujian.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled as governor of Fujian.

units.zh: 十年，法越事起，法艦窺台、閩。
units.en: In the tenth year the Franco-Vietnamese conflict broke out, and French warships probed Taiwan and Fujian.
units.literal: In the tenth year the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose and French warships probed Taiwan and Fujian.

units.zh: 張佩綸銜命會辦閩防軍務，兆棟畏其焰，曲意事之，日謁如衙參。
units.en: Zhang Peilun was commissioned to manage Fujian coastal defense. Zhaodong feared his power, deferred to him obsequiously, and called on him daily as if reporting to a superior.
units.literal: Zhang Peilun was commissioned to jointly manage Fujian coastal defense; Zhaodong feared his power, curried favor with him obsequiously, and called on him daily as if attending yamen duty.

units.zh: 佩綸虛飾胜狀，詔發萬金犒兆棟軍。
units.en: Peilun falsified reports of victory, and the court issued ten thousand taels to reward Zhaodong's troops.
units.literal: Peilun falsely dressed up reports of victory, and an edict issued ten thousand taels to reward Zhaodong's army.

units.zh: 兆棟且疏劾大員謀遁，意指何璟也，朝旨令據實以聞。
units.en: Zhaodong also memorialized that a senior official was plotting to flee—meaning He Jing—and the court ordered that the facts be reported truthfully.
units.literal: Zhaodong also memorialized impeaching a high official for plotting flight, meaning He Jing; the court ordered that the facts be reported truthfully.

units.zh: 已而事亟，己亦微服匿民間，數日略定，復出任事。
units.en: When crisis struck, he too went into disguise and hid among the people. After a few days the situation calmed somewhat and he resumed his duties.
units.literal: Before long affairs grew urgent; he too went in disguise and hid among the people; after several days things were somewhat settled and he resumed office.

units.zh: 璟罷，兆棟兼總督，朝廷論馬尾失守罪，褫職。
units.en: When Jing was dismissed, Zhaodong took over as acting governor. The court judged him guilty for the loss of Mawei and stripped him of office.
units.literal: When Jing was dismissed, Zhaodong concurrently acted as governor; the court judged guilt for the loss of Mawei and stripped him of office.

units.zh: 十三年，卒於閩。
units.en: He died in Fujian in the thirteenth year.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he died in Fujian.

units.zh: 宣統元年，复官。
units.en: In the first year of Xuantong his rank was posthumously restored.
units.literal: In the first year of Xuantong his office was posthumously restored.

units.zh: 論曰：法越初構釁，號識時務者爭上書忼慨言戰。
units.en: The historians comment: When the Franco-Vietnamese conflict first broke out, men who styled themselves statesmen vied in memorializing with passionate calls for war.
units.literal: The historians comment: When the Franco-Vietnamese conflict first arose, those who styled themselves men of insight vied in memorializing with passionate calls for war.

units.zh: 未及旬日，延旭敗退廣西，炯棄關外新安行營。
units.en: Within ten days Yanxu had been defeated and driven back to Guangxi, and Jiong had abandoned his headquarters beyond the border at Xin'an.
units.literal: Before ten days had passed, Yanxu was defeated and withdrew to Guangxi, and Jiong abandoned the field headquarters beyond the pass at Xin'an.

units.zh: 何璟、兆棟懾張佩綸之氣勢，怯懦而無所主，事急皆遁。
units.en: He Jing and Zhaodong were cowed by Zhang Peilun's authority—timid, irresolute, and quick to flee when crisis struck.
units.literal: He Jing and Zhaodong were overawed by Zhang Peilun's power; timid and without firm purpose, when affairs grew urgent they all fled.

units.zh: 方其互相汲引，不恤舉疆事以輕試；
units.en: When they had recommended one another, they did not hesitate to gamble the empire's frontier on a reckless trial;
units.literal: When they had recommended one another in turn, they did not hesitate to stake frontier affairs on a reckless trial;

units.zh: 及其敗也，其黨益肆言熒聽，而此數人者，遂得保首領以沒。
units.en: yet when they failed, their faction spread words to confuse the court, while these men kept their heads and died in bed.
units.literal: yet when they were defeated, their faction all the more spread words to confuse the court, while these several men were able to keep their heads and die in bed.

units.zh: 朝廷固寬大，亦失刑甚矣。
units.en: The court was magnanimous indeed—but it failed grievously in justice.
units.literal: The court was indeed magnanimous, but it also failed greatly in justice.
